definitions.explanation: A celestial event where numerous meteors are observed to radiate from a single point in the night sky, caused by the Earth passing through a trail of debris left by a comet.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今夜|こんや}→今夜：01411_konya⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}られる→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: You can see a meteor shower tonight.

examples.japanese: ペルセウス⟦{座|ざ}→座：28170_za⟧{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎年|まいとし}→毎年：00731_maitoshi⟧⟦{八月|はちがつ}→八月：00626_hachigatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見|み}られる→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: The Perseid meteor shower can be seen every year in August.

examples.japanese: ⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{行|い}って→行く：00119_iku⟧、{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{観察|かんさつ}する→観察する：21989_kansatsusuru⟧⟦つもり→つもり：01152_tsumori⟧だ。
examples.english: I plan to go up the mountain to observe the meteor shower.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{流星|りゅうせい}→流星：06310_ryuusei⟧ (meteor, shooting star) + ⟦{群|ぐん}→群：02790_gun⟧ (group, swarm). A word that appears frequently in news and conversation, especially during well-known annual meteor shower events.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {流星群|りゅうせいぐん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{観測|かんそく}→観測：00183_kansoku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to observe a meteor shower
- {流星群|りゅうせいぐん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{極大|きょくだい}→極大：20767_kyokudai⟧: the peak of a meteor shower
- {流星群|りゅうせいぐん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{見|み}ごろ: best viewing time for a meteor shower

WELL-KNOWN METEOR SHOWERS IN JAPAN:
- ペルセウス⟦{座|ざ}→座：28170_za⟧{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}: Perseid meteor shower (August)
- ふたご⟦{座|ざ}→座：28170_za⟧{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}: Geminid meteor shower (December)
- しぶんぎ⟦{座|ざ}→座：28170_za⟧{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}: Quadrantid meteor shower (January)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{流星|りゅうせい}→流星：06310_ryuusei⟧: meteor, shooting star
- ⟦{流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}→流れ星：05049_nagareboshi⟧: shooting star — the everyday, poetic term
- ⟦{彗星|すいせい}→彗星：05053_suisei⟧: comet — often the source of meteor shower debris
